Dukes Probate and Family Court: Your Comprehensive Guide

If you find yourself in need of legal services or assistance related to family matters in Dukes County, Massachusetts, Dukes Probate and Family Court is here to help. This court, located at 81 Main St., P.O. Box 237, Edgartown, MA 02539, is a vital resource for residents seeking resolution in family and probate cases. In this article, we will delve into everything you need to know about Dukes Probate and Family Court, from its services to accessibility, and how to get there.

Overview of Dukes Probate and Family Court

Dukes Probate and Family Court caters to all the towns within Dukes County. It's an essential institution for residents requiring legal assistance for family matters and probate cases. Whether you're dealing with divorce, child custody, or estate matters, this court has you covered.

Operating Hours

The court operates from Monday to Friday, ensuring accessibility throughout the workweek. Their hours are as follows:

  • Monday – Friday: 8:30 am – 4:30 pm

These hours are designed to accommodate a variety of schedules, making it easier for individuals to access the court's services when they need them most.

Parking Options

Conveniently, Dukes Probate and Family Court offers ample parking options for visitors. You can find a free parking lot located behind the courthouse, ensuring that you won't have to stress about finding a parking spot during your visit. Additionally, there's free street parking nearby, providing even more flexibility.

Public Transportation

If you prefer public transportation, the courthouse is easily accessible through various routes on the Vineyard Transit Authority, including Route 1, Route 6, Route 8, and Route 13. This transit-friendly approach ensures that you can reach the court conveniently, even without a personal vehicle.

Services Available

Dukes Probate and Family Court provides a range of services to meet your legal needs. Some of the key services offered include:

  • eFiling in the Probate and Family Court
  • Sign up for eReminder notifications for your court events

These services are designed to streamline your experience and ensure that you can navigate the legal process as efficiently as possible.

Accessibility

Ensuring accessibility for all visitors is a top priority for Dukes Probate and Family Court. If you require special accommodations due to the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), you can contact the ADA coordinator, Mallory Calamare, for more information:

  • Phone: (508) 627-4703
  • Fax: (508) 627-7664
  • Email: mallory.calamare@jud.state.ma.us

Mallory Calamare is available to assist you with any accessibility-related concerns or requirements you may have.

More Information

For additional information about Dukes Probate and Family Court, you can explore the following:

  • Judge's Lobby
    • Hon. Susan Jacobs, First Justice
  • Register's Office
    • Daphne Devries, Register

These resources can provide you with valuable insights and contacts within the court.

In conclusion, Dukes Probate and Family Court is a critical institution for residents of Dukes County, Massachusetts. With its comprehensive services, accessibility options, and accommodating operating hours, it ensures that individuals seeking legal assistance can navigate their family and probate matters efficiently. If you have any further questions or require assistance, don't hesitate to reach out to the court's dedicated staff.

Types of Court Case Records

Court case records are diverse, catering to different types of legal matters. Here's an overview of the main categories:

Superior Court Records

The Superior Court handles a wide range of cases, including civil, criminal, and family matters. Its records encompass a vast array of legal disputes, making them a valuable resource for researchers and legal professionals.

District Court Records

District Court records focus on cases that fall within specific geographic jurisdictions. These records are often accessible at the local level, making them crucial for individuals seeking information about cases in their communities.

Probate and Family Court Records

These records pertain to matters related to family law, including divorce, child custody, and probate proceedings. Accessing these records can be vital for those involved in family legal matters.

Housing Court Records

Housing Court records deal with disputes between landlords and tenants. These records can shed light on issues related to housing rights and responsibilities.

Land Court Records

The Land Court handles cases related to real estate and land ownership. Its records are essential for anyone dealing with property matters.

Boston Municipal Court Records

The Boston Municipal Court system focuses on cases within the city of Boston. These records are particularly useful for those residing in or dealing with legal matters in the Boston area.

Conclusion

Accessing court case records is a valuable skill in today's information age. Whether you're a legal professional, researcher, or simply someone interested in the workings of the judicial system, the ability to navigate and retrieve court records is an essential tool. From in-person visits to online databases and specialized court sessions, the options are diverse, catering to different needs and preferences.

By understanding the types of court records available and the various avenues for access, you can harness the power of information for your specific goals. Whether you're seeking legal forms, studying published opinions, or representing yourself in court, the resources and guidance provided here will help you navigate the complexities of the legal world.

Don't let the intricacies of the legal system deter you from obtaining the information you need. With the right knowledge and tools at your disposal, you can unlock the treasure trove of court case records and embark on a journey of discovery, research, and justice.

FAQs

1. Can I access court case records for free?

  • Yes, many court case records are available for free, either in-person at courthouses or through online databases. However, some records may require a fee for access.

2. Are court case records considered public information?

  • In most cases, court case records are considered public information and are accessible to the general public. However, there may be exceptions for certain sensitive or sealed records.

3. How can I search for historical court case records?

  • You can search for historical court case records by visiting the relevant courthouse or using online databases and archives that specialize in historical legal documents.

4. Can I request copies of court case records for my personal use?

  • Yes, in many cases, you can request copies of court case records for personal use. There may be fees associated with obtaining copies, and the process can vary by jurisdiction.

5. What types of legal forms can I find in court records?

  • Legal forms available in court records can include forms related to civil cases, family matters, probate proceedings, and more. Additionally, you may find forms that are not filed in court, such as tax forms and contracts.

6. What types of cases does Dukes Probate and Family Court handle?

  • Dukes Probate and Family Court handles a wide range of cases related to family matters and probate, including divorce, child custody, and estate matters.

7. Are there parking fees at the courthouse?

  • No, there are no parking fees at Dukes Probate and Family Court. They offer free parking both behind the courthouse and on nearby streets.

8. How can I receive notifications about my court events?

  • You can sign up for eReminder notifications to stay informed about your court events.

9. What public transportation options are available to reach the courthouse?

  • The courthouse is accessible via several Vineyard Transit Authority routes, including Route 1, Route 6, Route 8, and Route 13.

5. Who should I contact for accessibility-related concerns?

  • For ADA-related concerns, you can reach out to Mallory Calamare, the ADA coordinator, at (508) 627-4703 or mallory.calamare@jud.state.ma.us.
